name: Single wedge edge
description: Single wedge edge for edge diffraction (UTD), the first scene of the diffraction set. A 3 cm one-sided square light (radiance 10000) at z = 0.5 faces one black jaw whose edge lies along y at x = 0, z = 0. The jaw is a closed 2 cm slab spanning y in [-1.5, 1.5]; its edge is a 30 degree wedge, flat towards the light and bevelled towards the wall (exterior angle 330 degrees, UTD n = 11/6). A white Lambertian wall at z = -1 receives the light: lit for x < 0, in the jaw's shadow for x > 0, with the shadow boundary of the light's centre at x = 0. Diffraction makes fringes on the lit side and light inside the shadow. Design wavelength 5 mm; scale all lengths with it. The camera stands between the jaw and the wall, facing the wall.
